subject: Indigenous Languages
scopeNotes: Indigenous Languages is deliberately generic/language-agnostic in the KICD design itself: every 'Suggested Vocabulary' list, sample sentence, and all guidance text is written in ENGLISH, because Kenyan schools each teach their own local community's mother tongue (Kikuyu, Dholuo, Kalenjin, Kikamba, etc. — dozens of possibilities) and KICD does not prescribe which one. This matches the already-established, user-confirmed convention used for this project's existing Grade 7, 8, and 9 Indigenous Language builds (see curriculum.ts comments on g7-il-*/g8-il-*/il-* strands: 'generic-English-medium since KICD doesn't prescribe a single mother tongue'). Grade 6 skills are therefore built the same way: English-medium grammar/reading/writing-skill content, contextualised through the 9 official KICD themes, NOT vocabulary in any specific invented indigenous language.

Structurally Grade 6 differs from Grades 7-9: instead of one strand list of sub-strands each independently themed, Grade 6 is organised as 9 THEMES, each theme containing exactly 3 sub-strands — one per strand (1.x Listening and Speaking, 2.x/similar Reading, 3.x/similar Writing) — every sub-strand is 2 lessons. This mirrors the summary table's Listening and Speaking/Reading/Writing strand totals (18/18/18 = 54 lessons) plus 6 lessons of 'Showcasing concepts and skills' (not covered by generated practice skills, same treatment as other grades' non-testable showcase/CSL lessons).

27 sub-strands total (9 themes x 3 strands), each mapped 1:1 to one skill file — matching the French/Arabic/German G6 27-file precedent in file count, but themed by the 9 KICD Indigenous-Language themes (not language-learning vocabulary themes).

subStrands.title: Attentive Listening
outcomes: identify vocabulary from a story for comprehension
construct sentences using vocabulary and adverbs correctly for expression
cultivate attentive listening skills for effective communication
kiq: How do we demonstrate attentive listening?
When do we use adverbs?

subStrands.title: Reading for Information: Note Making
outcomes: identify key points in a text for information
summarise key information from a text for expression
appreciate the role of making summaries in reading
kiq: Why do we make notes?

subStrands.title: Handwriting
outcomes: identify features of a good handwriting for effective communication
re-write an essay using neat and legible handwriting for comprehension
appreciate neatness and legibility in handwriting
kiq: Why should we write legibly and neatly?

subStrands.title: Listening for Information: Active and passive voice

kiq: How do we use active and passive voice in sentences?

subStrands.title: Reading Fluency

subStrands.title: Mechanics of writing
